cases.rationale: Direct eval receives a function argument in an application-like preview flow.
limitations: Call reachability and caller control are not established.

cases.rationale: The direct Function constructor is in the configured syntactic rule scope, while its body is fixed.
limitations: The constructor does not establish attacker control or runtime reachability.

cases.rationale: A fixed literal is passed to direct eval.
limitations: Review priority depends on surrounding legacy execution context.

cases.rationale: Function(sourceText)() invokes the Function constructor without the new keyword; the current baseline rule explicitly matches eval(...) or new Function(...), so this syntax is outside its Rule Signal scope while still warranting code review.
limitations: Only the existing rule syntax is scored; equivalent dynamic-code behavior outside that syntax is tracked as a coverage gap. Runtime reachability and input provenance are not established.

cases.rationale: Direct eval appears in a configuration resolver.
limitations: Whether configuration is trusted is not established.

cases.rationale: Direct eval syntax is present with a constant expression.
limitations: Function execution and deployment context are unknown.

cases.rationale: The dangerous-looking text is only a line comment.
limitations: Comments are not evaluated as JavaScript.

cases.rationale: A method named eval returns data and does not invoke the global evaluator.
limitations: The method implementation is included, but wider callers are not.

cases.rationale: The token sequence is part of a template string.
limitations: No runtime template evaluation is inferred.

cases.rationale: JSON.parse is not a direct eval or Function-constructor pattern.
limitations: The meaning and validation of the parsed data are outside this rule.

cases.rationale: An alias to the Function constructor may execute dynamic code, but the configured pattern targets direct construction.
limitations: Alias resolution and actual invocation are outside the direct syntax rule.

cases.rationale: The evaluator is reached through a wrapper/helper shape not represented by the direct rule.
limitations: Actual call sites and input trust are not supplied.

cases.rationale: JSX passes a component property through the configured dangerous HTML attribute.
limitations: The property origin and any upstream sanitization are unknown.

cases.rationale: The exact JSX attribute pattern is present with a fixed literal.
limitations: The tool does not validate the literal or deployment context.

cases.rationale: The exact JSX sink receives a component property.
limitations: Runtime input provenance and sanitization are not proven.

cases.rationale: The sink is mediated through a prebuilt props object, outside the inline object pattern.
limitations: Component call sites and noticeText provenance are absent.

cases.rationale: A literal HTML value appears in the configured JSX sink shape.
limitations: No claim is made about the rendering policy or constant source.

cases.rationale: The rule matches the inline dangerous HTML property regardless of sanitizer naming.
limitations: The sanitizer implementation and its correctness are not provided.

cases.rationale: Ordinary React text interpolation is outside the dangerous HTML attribute rule.
limitations: Other rendering paths are not included.

cases.rationale: The property name is not React dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
limitations: Framework behavior beyond this JSX property is not evaluated.

cases.rationale: A non-React DOM sink may warrant review but is not the supported React JSX rule.
limitations: The DOM node origin and runtime use are unknown.

cases.rationale: React.createElement uses the dangerous property outside the configured JSX syntax.
limitations: The React runtime and value provenance are not analyzed.

cases.rationale: The input is rendered as text in JSX, without the configured HTML sink.
limitations: The application does not establish all other uses of html.

cases.rationale: A property flows to another component, but the receiving implementation is not supplied.
limitations: No sink exists in this file and component behavior is unavailable.

cases.rationale: A real allow declaration grants create under a literal true condition.
limitations: Deployment and effective inherited match scope are not checked.

cases.rationale: A nested real declaration includes write operations and literal true.
limitations: No deployed project or final access evaluation is available.

cases.rationale: A write permission is unconditionally allowed in a real rules file.
limitations: The target database and deployment status are unknown.

cases.rationale: This rule targets write permissions, while the declaration is read-only.
limitations: Whether public reading is acceptable depends on application policy.

cases.rationale: The update declaration has an authentication condition rather than literal true.
limitations: Authentication alone may not be sufficient authorization.

cases.rationale: The write-like text is commented out; the actual declaration is read-only.
limitations: Firestore lexical validation is bounded and does not compile rules.

cases.rationale: A write-like phrase is inside a string; actual permission is read-only.
limitations: String parsing does not establish deployability.

cases.rationale: Write permissions are conditional and do not match the literal-true target.
limitations: The full policy and identity assumptions are not evaluated.

cases.rationale: The content resembles a Firestore rules declaration but the supported path is firestore.rules.
limitations: The file type and deployment role cannot be established from content alone.

cases.rationale: The input is incomplete and lexical context does not establish a closed real declaration.
limitations: No Firebase parser or deployment validation is used.

cases.rationale: The write permission is explicitly false, not the configured literal true pattern.
limitations: Other allow declarations and parent conditions are absent.

cases.rationale: The declaration is conditional through a helper rather than literal true.
limitations: The helper and deployed policy semantics are not independently validated.

cases.rationale: The modeled query.code source reaches direct eval through a local alias.
limitations: The identifier req is syntactically modeled; HTTP origin, validation, route registration and reachability are unverified.

cases.rationale: The modeled body.code expression is passed directly to eval.
limitations: A variable named req is not proof of an actual request object.

cases.rationale: The declared Semgrep source is any object query.code, not only a framework request.
limitations: Actual external input provenance is not known.

cases.rationale: The base taint rule models this source-to-sink; the second rule models syntheticSafe as a sanitizer.
limitations: syntheticSafe is an evaluation-only assumption, not a validated sanitizer.

cases.rationale: The modeled source is read but is not passed to eval.
limitations: Other sinks outside this rule are not examined.

cases.rationale: The rule source is syntactic and matches this local object field.
limitations: This does not demonstrate a request or attacker-controlled value.

cases.rationale: A query field reaches eval but the configured source property is query.code.
limitations: No broader source modeling is performed.

cases.rationale: A modeled source is passed to an external helper whose implementation is unavailable.
limitations: Interprocedural reachability is not established.

cases.rationale: The taint source pattern uses an arbitrary receiver identifier with query.code.
limitations: The code may be a local job record; no request provenance is established.

cases.rationale: A modeled source crosses a helper boundary into a separate file.
limitations: The helper implementation and cross-file flow are not part of this case scan oracle.

cases.rationale: The modeled source is used as data without an eval sink.
limitations: The behavior of downstream consumers is not provided.

cases.rationale: The configured source-to-eval pattern is present and no modeled sanitizer is used.
limitations: normalize implementation and external input source are unknown.

cases.rationale: The configured request field flows into the first argument of child_process.exec under supported require syntax.
limitations: Actual HTTP reachability and shell behavior are not executed.

cases.rationale: The modeled body.cmd is passed to the first execSync argument using supported namespace import.
limitations: Caller reachability and runtime authorization are unknown.

cases.rationale: A supported named alias sink receives a command string containing the modeled field.
limitations: Quoting and execution context are not validated.

cases.rationale: The supported sink receives a constant and contains no modeled taint source.
limitations: The command’s effect and runtime access are not evaluated.

cases.rationale: RegExp.exec is not a child_process sink.
limitations: No shell API is present in the fixture.

cases.rationale: The modeled field occurs only in the options argument, not the command string.
limitations: Other execution option risks are outside this rule’s command-string target.

cases.rationale: The input reaches an API outside the configured exec/execSync sink set.
limitations: spawn options such as shell behavior are not assessed.

cases.rationale: The modeled input is passed to a helper with no implementation in the scanned case.
limitations: No child_process call is included in this fixture.

cases.rationale: The value reaches a supported-like sink, but query.term is not a modeled source.
limitations: No broader request-property source modeling is claimed.

cases.rationale: The object shadows the module name and is not imported from child_process.
limitations: Static scope resolution and test intent are not evaluated.

cases.rationale: A module alias is used, but the supported namespace variable name is child_process.
limitations: Alias identity and runtime path are outside configured patterns.

cases.rationale: A value is passed to a separate service with no implementation in this case.
limitations: Whether the service invokes a shell is unavailable.
